issues.legal_issue: The statutory eviction framework could not be held unconstitutional in light of the applicable Supreme Court precedent.
material_facts: An eviction order under a public-lands eviction statute was affirmed on appeal.
The High Court, relying on a Full Bench decision, held the statute unconstitutional in its entirety and set aside the eviction order on that ground alone.
In the appeal before the Supreme Court, counsel for both sides agreed that an earlier Supreme Court decision meant the statute could not be regarded as unconstitutional.
Other points in the revision petition remained undecided.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the statute could not be deemed unconstitutional, allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court judgment, and remanded the matter to the High Court to decide the remaining revision points.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the dictum in Maganlal Chhaganlal (P.) Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay, the Court held that the U.P. Public Lands (Eviction and Recovery of Rent and Damages) Act, 1959 could not be deemed unconstitutional. The High Court had relied on Raja Ram Verma v. State of U.P., but that view did not govern the Supreme Court's decision. The judgment identifies no specific statutory provision as the basis for the ruling.

predicates.appeal_from_revision_judgment: A party brings an appeal from a High Court judgment deciding a challenge to an eviction order through revision.
predicates.high_court_invalidated_entire_eviction_l: The High Court held the eviction law unconstitutional in its entirety and set aside the eviction order on that ground.
predicates.prior_supreme_court_precedent_addressed_: An earlier Supreme Court decision addressed the constitutionality of the relevant kind of eviction law.
predicates.parties_agreed_precedent_applied: The parties agreed that the earlier Supreme Court decision governed the validity issue.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a revision judgment involves a High Court decision invalidating an entire eviction law, and an applicable prior Supreme Court decision is agreed to govern, the eviction law is not treated as unconstitutional.
